name: Electric Bicycle
description: A two- or three-wheeled vehicle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal-assist to 20 mph, throttle-capable to 20 mph, or pedal-assist to 28 mph. Defined by West Virginia Code §17C-1-70 and regulated by §17C-11-8, both last amended by HB 2062 (2023).

restrictions.rule: Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; Class 2 may use a throttle to propel the bike but can't assist past 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
Two or three wheels, fully operable pedals, and a motor of fewer than 750 watts
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512), and the motor stops propelling it when the rider stops pedaling or brakes
A Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour

Must not be tampered with or modified to change its motor-powered speed or its pedal-assist or throttle engagement; one modified past the limits is no longer an electric bicycle, except when ridden only on the owner's own property
Riders and passengers under 15 must wear a bicycle helmet, under the Child Bicycle Safety Act
No riding under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances
Class 1 and Class 2 have a traditional bicycle's rights and duties on roads and trails, including public lands, wherever traditional bicycles are allowed
A Class 3 may not ride on a bicycle path, multi-use trail or single-use trail unless it's within a highway or roadway, or the municipality, local authority or state agency that manages it allows it
Never allowed anywhere traditional bicycles are prohibited; private property owners may allow or restrict it
No registration, title, driver's license or insurance
